card.stem: A dwelling house has an open-plan kitchen and dining area on the ground floor, as shown. The kitchen has a solid concrete floor with a 20 mm tile finish. rows.contextNote: Best eight points, 4 each (drawing 3, annotation 1). card.questionText: When specifying a high performance external wall for a new house, a choice is to be made between: a rendered cavity wall of concrete block construction or a wall of timber frame construction with a rainscreen of cedar cladding, as shown or a rendered wall of timber frame and hemp-lime construction. Select any two of the above wall types, and using notes and freehand sketches, show the typical design detailing for each wall type selected. Name the typical components of each wall and include typical dimensions.

rows.verbatim: Choice of high performance wall (any two)
rows.contextNote: Any two of the three printed wall types, each note 5, sketch 5 and dimensions 2 = 12. Concrete block construction: a cavity that prevents moisture ingress; full-fill insulation; internal render for airtightness; strong, robust blocks; durable, weather-resistant external plaster. Timber frame construction: T&G cedar or lapped larch or Douglas fir on counter battens for weatherproofing and ventilation; a moisture-resistant layer; OSB/plywood racking; full-fill insulation in the frame; an internal airtightness layer and service cavity. Timber frame and hemp-lime construction: hempcrete sprayed or cast 300–500 mm thick around a structural timber frame; Heraklith boards at openings; two coats of internal render; an external leaf of hempcrete and hemp-lime render.

card.stem: The external wall of a house built in the 1970s is of single-leaf, hollow-block construction with an external render. Plasterboard, with bonded expanded polystyrene, is fixed to the internal surface of the wall, as shown.
card.questionText:
Calculate the U-value of the external wall, given the following data: External render thickness 16 mm; Hollow concrete block thickness 215 mm; Expanded polystyrene thickness 25 mm; Plasterboard thickness 12.5 mm.
Thermal data of external wall of house: Resistance of external surface (R) 0.048 m2 °C/W; Resistivity of external render (r) 2.170 m °C/W; Resistance of concrete block (R) 0.210 m2 °C/W; Conductivity of expanded polystyrene (k) 0.037 W/m °C; Conductivity of plasterboard (k) 0.160 W/m °C; Resistance of internal surface (R) 0.104 m2 °C/W.

rows.contextNote: The calculation set out in a table of material, conductivity, resistivity, thickness and resistance.

rows.verbatim: External surface resistance External render Hollow block Polystyrene Plasterboard Internal surface resistance
rows.contextNote: Six resistances, 3 each: external surface 0.048 (given); render 0.016 × 2.170 = 0.03472; hollow block 0.210 (given); polystyrene 0.025/0.037 = 0.67568; plasterboard 0.0125/0.160 = 0.078125; internal surface 0.104 (given). All in m²°C/W.
Total resistance Rt = 1.151 m²°C/W.

rows.verbatim: U-Value of external wall (1 mark for formula)
rows.contextNote: U = 1 ÷ Rt = 1 ÷ 1.151 = 0.869 W/m²°C (1 mark for the formula).

card.stem: While there are undoubtedly many buildings whose heritage values dictate that they should be preserved unchanged, the reality is that few are of such importance that they and their settings are not capable of being remodelled to accommodate new uses - especially where they have outlived the functions for which they were constructed, and where adaptation and reuse is the most viable option for extending their lifespans and preserving the vitality of their urban locations.
